audit.whatIsWrong: The page invented a terrain mechanic Ryze does not have and repeated it five times: 'any wall-root setup he tries' (whys[2], content early), 'Watch for E-wall setups near river bushes' (content mid), 'Look for E-wall root combos near lane terrain' (wants.foe[1]), 'his Q-Q root setups, especially near walls' (wants.you[1]), and 'once he is 3-4 items deep with a wall to isolate you' (spikes[3].text).
audit.why: Nothing in Ryze's kit interacts with walls. Rune Prison is 615 range and 'traps a target in a cage of runes, damaging them and slowing their movement. If the target has Flux on it, they are instead rooted.' The root condition is Spell Flux on the target, full stop. A reader watching walls is watching the wrong thing and will eat the root every time.
audit.corrected: The real trigger is now the stated tell in nine fields: no Flux, no root — Rune Prison is only a slow without it. The E is 615 range and 3.5s at rank 1, so breaking the chain at the E is the counterplay.

audit.whatIsWrong: The lane's difficulty was framed as 'point-blank root' and as a mana-starvation matchup with no numbers.
audit.why: Rune Prison is 615 range, not point-blank, and Overload reaches 1000 on a 5-second cooldown that his other spells reset. What actually gates him is that both 615-range spells force him to step into your 900.
audit.corrected: Ranges and cooldowns supplied in tldr, winCon, breakdown.early, whys[1] and content early: he reaches 1000 with the Q but has to close to 615 to start the chain.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike was written as 'Between Worlds gives a repositioning and execute tool' (spikes[1].text) and 'a clean disengage and execute his Realm Warp can't answer' (whys[3]).
audit.why: Aurora's R has no execute — 'a shockwave that damages and slows... she creates an area that slows enemies within it and allows Aurora to teleport from one side of the area to the other'. Realm Warp is 3000 range on 180/160/140 and 'After a few seconds, allies standing near the portal are teleported' — a map tool with a delay, not a duel answer either way.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten to what the two ultimates actually are: a slow field with a teleport across it, against a delayed 3000-unit portal for his team.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit — defect-catalogue item 3 — and dosFull[2].d invented one, calling the post-Rune-Prison window a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Rune Prison is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9. Fifteen seconds is not a rank of it, so a reader committing on that number arrives after the root is back.
audit.corrected: Real numbers: W 11s at rank 1, 615 range; E 3.5s at rank 1 down to 2.5s at rank 5; Q 5s at 1000 with resets off his other spells; your W 22s. The invented figure is gone.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string under a spirit-haste title, dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string under 'Stand in his rotation during E cooldown', and dontsFull[0].d called a single male enemy 'they'. spikes[0].text and content early also carried the fabricated Aurora ability name 'Twin Drift'.
audit.why: Copy-paste bleed (defect item 2) plus a fabricated name that matches nothing in the kit file.
audit.corrected: Bodies rewritten to answer their own titles; the fabricated name removed and replaced with the slot letter and the real 900 range rather than a guessed name.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] and spikes[2].text built on 'Riftmaker/Shadowflame' and 'Riftmaker or Shadowflame' while report[8] says Luden's into Sorcerer's, then Shadowflame and Rabadon's.
audit.why: Two builds on one page, and the slash form is placeholder phrasing.
audit.corrected: Aligned to the page's own itemization. I also dropped the specific claim about which items Ryze needs (Seraph's and 'a Rod') where I was rewriting, and replaced it with the mechanic that is actually in the kit: his passive converts bonus mana into damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: LEVEL CHART DISAGREEMENT, LEFT ALONE DELIBERATELY. phases[].side reads [Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Skill, Skill, Ryze, Ryze] while content win[0..6] all read 'Aurora' — four rows disagreeing across the two layers.
audit.why: I cannot resolve it. packet.levelChart says Aurora x7 and win[] agrees, but the full layer's later rows say Ryze, and the page's own content late and spikes[3] describe the matchup flipping once he has three items — an account that is coherent with phases[5]/[6] and with a 50.52% win rate over 859 games. Nothing in the kit tells me whether a three-item Ryze beats a three-item Aurora. Chart edits are validated as an atomic group, so I could not fix half of it either.
audit.corrected: No side, no rating, no win[] edit. Recorded in questionsForUser. I deliberately KEPT the late-game prose that says the matchup can flip, because that is the reading I would bet on and overwriting it would have destroyed information while the rows stayed broken anyway.

audit.why: 50.52% over 859 games; diff EVEN at 5.5/10 matches it. No edit.

notes: A MECHANIC THAT DOES NOT EXIST, REPEATED FIVE TIMES. whys[2], content early, content mid, wants.you[1], wants.foe[1] and spikes[3].text all told the reader to watch for Ryze's 'wall-root' setups near terrain. Ryze's kit has no terrain interaction of any kind. Rune Prison slows; it roots ONLY if the target already has Spell Flux on them. That is the whole trigger, it is in Riot's own text, and it is the single most useful thing this page could tell an Aurora player. A reader watching walls eats the root every time. Every one of those fields now names Flux as the tell. TWO FABRICATIONS KILLED: 'Twin Drift' for Aurora's Q (whys[2], spikes[0].text, content early, wants.you[1]) — fifth matchup in my slice carrying this invented name, so it is a file-wide problem, not a per-matchup one. And 'execute' attributed to Between Worlds twice (whys[3], spikes[1].text) — Aurora's R damages and slows and creates a teleport zone; there is no execute in her kit. Neither was replaced with a guessed name; the kit file carries no Aurora ability names, so I used slot letters and real ranges. INVENTED NUMBER REMOVED: dosFull[2].d offered a 'fifteen-second invitation' after Rune Prison. It is 11s at rank 1 and 9s at rank 5 — the reader was being sent in against a root that was already back. PACKET SUSPECT IS A FALSE POSITIVE: 'Your Between Worlds' was flagged, but Between Worlds is Aurora's real R name. I edited that field for the execute error, not for the name. CHART LEFT ALONE ON PURPOSE: phases[].side reads [Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Skill, Skill, Ryze, Ryze] against win[] Aurora x7. packet.levelChart says Aurora x7, but the page's own content late and spikes[3] describe the matchup flipping at three items, which agrees with the full layer and with a 50.52% win rate. I could not tell which is right from the kit, chart edits are atomic so a partial fix would be held back anyway, and I kept the flip-late prose because that is the more defensible reading. Needs a human call; see questionsForUser.
